extracted.intended_audience: Researchers invited to peer review manuscripts for PLOS journals
extracted.subtask_description: Checklist for researchers performing peer review of journal manuscripts, covering actions to take when invited, how to read a manuscript, and how to write the review report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirm the manuscript is in your area of expertise
rubrics_metrics.description: Confirm the manuscript is in your area of expertise
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action to take when you’re invited to review — accept only if you have appropriate subject-matter expertise to assess the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make sure you have enough time
rubrics_metrics.description: Make sure you have enough time
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action to take when you’re invited to review — ensure you can complete a careful review by the journal’s deadline before accepting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check for competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: Check for competing interests
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Action to take when you’re invited to review — identify any conflicts of interest that would preclude impartial review and disclose them to the journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify the research question and key claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the research question and key claims
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary reading task — determine what the paper aims to address and what central conclusions or claims the authors make.

rubrics_metrics.name: Think about context and related literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Think about context and related literature
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary reading task — assess whether the work is placed appropriately within existing literature and whether relevant prior work is considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Look at the figures and tables. Are they clear? Do they represent what the study is about?
rubrics_metrics.description: Look at the figures and tables. Are they clear? Do they represent what the study is about?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary reading task — evaluate clarity, labeling, and whether figures/tables appropriately illustrate the data and support the study’s objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine the results. Are they supported by the data?
rubrics_metrics.description: Examine the results. Are they supported by the data?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary reading task — check that analyses and results follow from the data and that claims are justified by the presented evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Read the conclusions. Do they make sense?
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the conclusions. Do they make sense?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary reading task — verify that conclusions are logical given the results and avoid overstating implications beyond the evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check the methods. Are they appropriate and reproducible?
rubrics_metrics.description: Check the methods. Are they appropriate and reproducible?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary reading task — assess whether methods are suitable to answer the research question and described sufficiently for reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review the journal guidelines and publication criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Review the journal guidelines and publication criteria
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary reading task — ensure the manuscript conforms to the journal’s editorial policies, formatting, and publication criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Keep everything confidential!
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep everything confidential!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary reading task / ethical duty — do not share manuscript content or use results before publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start with a summary of the research
rubrics_metrics.description: Start with a summary of the research
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing the report — begin the review by succinctly summarizing the study and its main findings to show you understood the work.

rubrics_metrics.name: State your overall impression
rubrics_metrics.description: State your overall impression
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing the report — provide a clear high-level evaluation (e.g., major strengths/weaknesses, suitability for publication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Number your comments and separate them into “major” and “minor” issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Number your comments and separate them into “major” and “minor” issues
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing the report — organize feedback clearly so editors/authors can distinguish critical concerns from smaller points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give concrete examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Give concrete examples
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing the report — support critiques with specific examples from the manuscript rather than vague statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refer to specific sections and page numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: Refer to specific sections and page numbers
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing the report — cite exact locations in the manuscript to help authors find and address issues efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Don’t focus on spelling and grammar
rubrics_metrics.description: Don’t focus on spelling and grammar
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing the report — prioritize substantive scientific issues over minor copyediting; note major language problems only if they impede understanding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be professional and respectful
rubrics_metrics.description: Be professional and respectful
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing the report — maintain a constructive and courteous tone in critiques to facilitate improvement and collegial discourse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate if you’re available to look at the revised version
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate if you’re available to look at the revised version
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing the report — tell the editor whether you are willing to review a revision, aiding editorial planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include positive feedback too!
rubrics_metrics.description: Include positive feedback too!
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing the report — acknowledge strengths of the manuscript as well as weaknesses to provide balanced feedback.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finish on time
rubrics_metrics.description: Finish on time
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When writing the report / overall duty — submit the review by the deadline to support timely editorial decisions.
